newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Undervalued region shares to lead Russian bull run.
newsitem.headline: Undervalued region shares to lead Russian bull run.

text.p: Experienced Russian investors are moving into undervalued regional shares and new funds are flowing into leading issues, keeping the whole market on course for new records, traders and analysts said on Friday.

Hedge funds, brokers and other investors who have been in the Russian market for a year or more are moving money into secondary shares, making quick windfalls as the market follows their attention and revalues them.
"Every day you see a regional telecom or energo (utility) shoot up like a star," said one senior trader, who believes that obscure stocks would continue to lead the market.

The RTS 24-share index has risen more than 50 percent this year, and on Friday continued to close in on its record high of 312.66. At midday on Friday the market was trading at 310.78, up slightly from 310.63 on Thursday.
But on most days this year the biggest winners on the Russian Trading System (RTS) have been among around 90 telecoms and 90 utilities, which can rise by 20 percent or so in a single day.
Regional utility Chelyabenergo CHNG.RTS, which traded at $0.450 on Thursday, has risen from a 1997 low of $0.198, but has traded only 10 times in the last 10 days.
The extremely illiquid shares bounce up on re-evaluation, independent of a company's growth potential.
"So it goes -- every day someone comes with new money and that has a big effect on the secondary shares. People do not care about fundamentals," the trader said.
But leading shares have not suffered from outflows.

"There are a few more sellers (of leading shares) than in January, because some of those who have been in the market a couple of years are restructuring," said Alfa Capital deputy director of international sales Alexei Genkin.
"But there are very limited volumes on the offer side."
Gavin Rankin, head of research at Troika Dialog brokerage, said that the reallocations represented a small pool of funds.

"If you look at January, 52 percent of all trading was done in five stocks," he said, adding that February would probably be similar. The top 10 shares accounted for 78 percent of deals in dollar terms on the Russian Trading System, he said.

Traders said short-term investors and brokers go to the regions to buy shares, and by bringing them back to Moscow raise liquidity. This allows a share price to stabilise and spreads to narrow after initial spectacular growth.
But Rankin, who estimated the market would show 10 percent appreciation per month this year, said most trading would remain in a limited number of shares.
"There are a substantial number of exciting telecoms and energos, but liquidity remains a big problem," he said.
"Longer term investors are not able to source sufficient stock for their positions."

Traders and analysts said preferred shares, which offer no voting rights but a guaranteed dividend and trade at a big discount to ordinaries, had the potential to show secondary share growth and the liquidity of leading company stocks.

Preferred shares of oil firm LUKoil LKOH.RTS 0#LKOH.RUO had risen to $12.91 midday on Friday from $12.60 at Thursday's close. Trade began on Thursday in its American Depositary Receipt programme, which allows foreign trading of the shares.
Rankin said the top five prefs already accounted for 13 percent of trade on the RTS, and that discounts could decrease.
"They could close the discount gap entirely," he said.
